clue.text: Shake tower of strength

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sway or move violently back and forth
second meaning: a dependable person others lean on

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rattle a person everyone relies on.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to shake a strong tower; the verb and the noun phrase are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to sway violently, as an earthquake does; the noun is a firm, reliable supporter, a person you can lean upon.

clue.text: Cancel article in disgust

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside that other word

explanation.surface: Someone angrily withdraws a piece of writing they find offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside REPEL, between its P and E, to give REPEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke it formally, so the verb is a synonym for annul or scrap.

clue.text: Approach keeping fringes of hair yellow

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it within its own letters
the fringes of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of hair

explanation.surface: Advice on dyeing, where the ends of the hair turn yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Chrome yellow is a bright pigment, which is why the word alone can name the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is short for chrome yellow, a vivid pigment from lead chromate used by painters and printers.

clue.text: Fellow enthralled by complicated maths, no novelist

indicators.note: a thing enthralled by another is held captive inside it
something complicated is tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man captivated by tricky maths is clearly no writer of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No novelist' looks like a single phrase, but 'no' belongs to the anagram fodder and only 'novelist' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann was the German author of The Magic Mountain and Buddenbrooks, a Nobel-winning writer of long fiction.

clue.text: Spanish article supporting fashionable guest house

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

explanation.surface: A Spanish piece of writing backs a trendy place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the supporting piece is the lower one, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment offering rooms and meals to paying visitors, much like a larger lodging house.

clue.text: Travelling merchant hurt company with game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A roving trader damages a firm through some sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian trader who journeyed to China and the court of Kublai Khan in the thirteenth century.

clue.text: Sign of fortitude, having quarrel with superior in error

indicators.note: the pieces being in another word means they are placed inside it

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake

indicators.note: with simply joins one piece on after the other

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Showing courage despite a mistaken row with one's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The stiff upper lip is the British ideal of keeping emotions hidden under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a stiff upper lip is the British idiom for staying stoical and unemotional in the face of hardship.

clue.text: Judges in time consumed by bias err badly

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it
done badly means done wrongly, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Referees, given time, let their prejudice lead them into mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of bias err are rearranged and T goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter settles disputes with authority, so the plural is a synonym for adjudicators or referees.

clue.text: Negative methods receiving notice in these times

indicators.note: a word receiving another takes it in among its own letters

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Pessimistic approaches get attention in the modern world.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at the present time, contrasting today with the past, exactly as the phrase about current times does.

clue.text: Level still without one floor covering

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A flat, motionless floor that lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIET loses its I to give QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquet is flooring of wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern, so it covers a floor.

clue.text: One doing less well than expected, suffering ruin, ached continually

definitions.text: One doing less well than expected

indicators.note: suffering words are damaged and knocked out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disappointing performer whose ruin brings constant pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An underachiever performs below their ability or below what others predicted, the very description in the clue.

clue.text: Colourful display in fantastic bar I own

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imagined, so these letters are reshaped into something new

parts.note: three words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub landlord boasts of the brilliant light show at their place.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is the arc of spectral colours seen when sunlight passes through raindrops, a vivid show in the sky.

clue.text: Run into a wild, rough old animal

indicators.note: going into a word means being placed inside it

parts.note: a taken as written, and wild means mad
the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a savage, ageing, shaggy beast.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into A MAD after the A. Rough as a description of the animal looks like the definition, but it means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is a burrowing American mammal protected by bony plates, so it is an animal by example.

clue.text: Certain alien back in fashion

indicators.note: one word in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word is read from its end

explanation.surface: A particular extraterrestrial is trendy again.
explanation.walkthrough: Certain looks like a qualifier for alien but is the definition, in the sense of bound to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fated is destined by fate, so it is sure to happen, which is one sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Artist, good artist with clarity, finally sad about broken pen

indicators.note: one word about another wraps around it
finally points to the very end of the word, so only its last letter is kept
something broken is smashed into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clear-sighted painter is upset about a broken pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'artist' twice: the first defines, the second is RA, a member of the Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grayson Perry is the English potter and Turner Prize winner known for ceramics, tapestries and cross-dressing alter ego Claire.

clue.text: Beatles song certainly rated uncommonly higher than unknown quantity

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is higher than another piece comes before it
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so these letters are placed in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Beatles number is surely rated more highly than a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is the 1965 Paul McCartney ballad recorded by the Beatles, among the most covered pop songs.

clue.text: Day in season, endlessly cheerful, described concisely

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A summer's day spent in constant good spirits, captured in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes into SUMMER before its R, and that R is then cut off, leaving SUMMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum up is to give a brief overview, so something summed up has been put into few words.

clue.text: Sailor breaking rule or prepared to give a hand?

indicators.note: a word breaking another bursts into the middle of it
prepared means made up or worked over, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a seaman who flouts the regulations still willing to help out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared to give a hand' looks like the definition, but prepared works on the letters and only 'a hand' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand or factory hand, so a labourer fits.

clue.text: Not familiar with upper-class conduct, same all over the place

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is not used to posh manners, which seem identical and chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaccustomed to something means having no experience of it, so you are not used to it.

clue.text: Beautiful guess

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to work something out by intuition

explanation.walkthrough: An adjective and a verb that happen to share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally divine means delightful or gorgeous; as a verb it means to discover by insight, as a guess does.

clue.text: Refuse to accept hard defeat

indicators.note: a word that accepts another takes it into itself

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take a heavy loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse looks like a verb, to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash an opponent is to beat them heavily, so the verb is an informal synonym for trounce.

clue.text: One with force reflected about love for language

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror runs the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
with simply joins one piece on after the other
one word about another goes around it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone forceful turns around for love of a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces are joined before being read backwards, and only then wrapped around love. Love is zero in tennis scoring, hence the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Maori is the Polynesian tongue of New Zealand's indigenous people, an official language there alongside English.

clue.text: Sorry about thousand libels, criminally elaborate

indicators.note: one word about others goes around them

parts.note: eh? is what you say when you ask someone to repeat themselves

indicators.note: criminally means wrongly or unlawfully, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An apology about vast defamation that was wickedly exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: Sorry here is the question 'Sorry?' asked by someone who has misheard, which is EH, not an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to add decoration or detail, so as a verb elaborate is a close synonym.

clue.text: Stop working for lord

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An instruction to cease labouring on behalf of a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage, addressed as Lord, so he is a nobleman.

clue.text: Energy in motivation daughter gained

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

explanation.surface: A daughter acquired vigour and ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something derived has been obtained or drawn from a source, so it matches gained as a past participle.

clue.text: Model army's leader after survival seizing power

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other
a word seizing another grabs it and holds it inside

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only its first letter is kept

explanation.surface: A military figure, having outlasted all, takes over government.
explanation.walkthrough: Survival here is a noun for a thing that has survived from the past, not the act of surviving.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy, so a scale model of something is one kind of it.

clue.text: Painting left strangely grainy

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A canvas was abandoned looking oddly textured.
explanation.walkthrough: Painting reads as a noun for the picture but is the verb form, depicting.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraying means depicting someone in a picture or words, so painting in the sense of representing is a synonym.

clue.text: Network becomes helpful to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just a part of the words is used

parts.note: sitting across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A web of contacts proves partly useful.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net of interlaced strands, so it is a synonym for a network of connected threads.
